chapter_title: The Three Earths that Exist, they bear Fruit.
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:**
Three degrees of the mind exist within the whole created order of the human being, and all three are undergoing regeneration. At first they [GAP-1] resist the Divine intelligence that labors within them, as unbroken ground resists the one who would sow. Afterwards they bring forth [GAP-2: REVIEW — genuine works of charity] to the Divine powers that labor upon them.

**¶2:**
One of these is the outermost natural mind, upon which all merely sensory and worldly thought resides. The Divine works to break open this hardened natural plane [GAP-3], penetrating it with truths on the lowest natural level — for iron implements correspond to the hard discipline of natural truth applied by effort — and orders it into receptive arrangements [GAP-4: REVIEW — forming orderly states capable of receiving seeds of interior truth], overturning its former self-derived orientation [GAP-5]. Afterwards good works are gathered from [GAP-6: this reformed natural mind], which now yields what it could not yield before.

**¶3:**
The second degree is the interior spiritual mind, the living and sacred plane of consciousness. It is dispersed and intermingled throughout every region of existence, in higher states and in lower. The intelligences that labor upon it are the two great principles of Divine love and Divine wisdom, which proceed through all the interior heavens of the mind. They labor and cultivate this spiritual plane so that they may draw whatever is receptive of good and truth toward their own likeness. And the spiritual mind, so vivified, rises up and ascends to elevated states of perception. It goes upward, liberated from every condition of mixture and captivity in which it had been held, and in ascending it augments the heavenly kingdom — adding itself to what is Divine.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Three earths exist in the universe, and are being toiled over. At first they [trouble] the farmer in them. Afterwards they bear [good] fruit to they who toil over them.

One of them is this great earth that people are living upon. They are ploughing in it [and digging], it with iron hoes, they cultivate, [making] the furrows, turning it over [from its place] Afterwards they harvest fruit from [it in its season]

The second field is the living soul, the holy one. It is mixed in the entire zone, above and below. The farmers who toil over it are these two great light-givers, which journey through the heavens. They are toiling and cultivating it, so that they will draw it towards their aspect. And it leaps up and comes to the heights. It goes upwards, out from every place wherein it is, and it adds to them.

fills.explanation: Uncultivated ground resists and troubles the farmer who works it; this corresponds to the unregenerate mind resisting the Divine intelligence that labors within it.
The editor's "good" is confirmed: "good fruit" corresponds precisely to genuine works of charity produced after regeneration, standard vocabulary in the Kephalaia's agricultural parables.

The spiritual reading calls for "breaking open the hardened natural plane" at this position; digging with iron hoes is the natural-register action that breaks open hard ground, and it pairs naturally with the ploughing that precedes it.

The editor's "making" is confirmed: "making the furrows" corresponds to forming orderly receptive states in the natural mind, and is the standard agricultural term for this action in the Kephalaia register.
Turning soil "from its place" corresponds to overturning the mind's former self-derived orientation — displacing the natural arrangement so that a new, divinely-ordered one can be established.

The reformed natural mind yields fruit "in its season" — a standard agricultural and scriptural formula expressing that after the labor of regeneration, good works are produced at the appointed time of maturation.
